Priya Rao: Quick handoff — noticed a small SLO blip in eu-west around ~02:20 UTC. KV cache eviction spike caused a short (~1min) burst of 5xxs from the batcher. I rolled back the canary and started warming the cache. Logs: https://internal/logs/incident-5612347 :eyes:
ops-bot: [ALERT] eu-west batcher 5xx spike (02:20–02:21 UTC) — severity: warning — alert_id: alert-euw-5612
Ben K.: Thanks — any idea which rollout touched evictions? do we have a PR/commit?
Priya Rao: Looks tied to model-serve canary (v2.3.1). Rolled canary back to v2.3.0 at 02:28 UTC. Ran `scripts/kv_warmup.sh --region=eu-west` and bumped batcher `max_concurrency` to 8 temporarily. Monitoring metrics now, error rate falling.
Noah W.: Can you paste the PR/commit and open a ticket for follow-ups? I'll pick up the runbook update. Also pinging @eng-runtime to check kernel selection behavior under eviction bursts.
Priya Rao: PR: https://git/repo/changes/1234 · commit 9f2c8b2. Created SRE-1987 for the follow-up (root cause, canary gating, improved warmup). Assigned to Ben. Added a short note to the runbook: "if eu-west KV evictions correlate with canary deploys, rollback + warmup + increase debounce".
Lina M.: Oncall question — should we widen the alert debounce window or tune thresholds before next deploy?
Priya Rao: I bumped debounce for that alert from 60s -> 180s for the next 24h while we triage. If it continues we'll set a temporary suppression and escalate to postmortem. :thumbsup:
Ben K.: Taking SRE-1987, will do a quick CR review for the canary gating change and follow up tomorrow AM. Thanks for the rapid rollback and notes.
